question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=5$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5 & =1-\frac{{5}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{5}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{5}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯ \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡5 & =1-\frac{25}{2!}+\frac{625}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{5}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\operatorname{cos}⁡5.$
